chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Yahya ibn Abi Imran, from Yunus, from Is'haq ibn Ammar, who said:

I asked one of the two Imams (peace be upon them) about the penalty (Hadd) of the speechless, the deaf, and the blind, so he (peace be upon him) said: 'The penalties are upon them, when they have the intellect for what they do.'

key_terms.حَدّ: Penalty (specifically fixed punishments for specific crimes)

ai.seo_question: Are deaf, blind, or speechless people exempt from Islamic penalties (Hudud)?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, Shaykh al-Kulayni records this narration from Isma'il ibn 'Ammar, where he asks one of the Imams (peace be upon them) regarding the legal status of those with sensory impairments. The Imam clarifies that the application of Hudud (fixed Islamic penalties) depends on 'aql' (intellect/cognitive capacity) rather than sensory perfection, establishing that deaf, dumb, or blind individuals are fully liable for their actions if they possess mental competence. This principle underscores the Shia juristic view that the essence of legal responsibility lies in the mind's ability to comprehend and intend, not merely in the physical organs of perception.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Yahya Bin Abu Imran, from Yunus, from Is’haq Bin Ammar who said,

‘I asked one of the two (5th or 6th Imamasws) about a Penalty (Hadd) of the speechless, the deaf and the blind, so heasws said: ‘Upon them are the Penalties, when they they have the intellect of what they are coming to’.
